title: Maximize the Distance Between Points on a Square
summary: Given an integer side representing the edge length of a square with corners at (0, 0), (0, side), (side, 0), and (side, side) on a Cartesian plane, and a positive integer k along with a 2D integer array points where each point is represented as [xi, yi] on the boundary of the square, select k points such that the minimum Manhattan distance between any two points is maximized.
statement: Given an integer side representing the edge length of a square with corners at (0, 0), (0, side), (side, 0), and (side, side) on a Cartesian plane, and a positive integer k along with a 2D integer array points where each point is represented as [xi, yi] on the boundary of the square, select k points such that the minimum Manhattan distance between any two points is maximized. Return the maximum possible minimum Manhattan distance between the selected k points. The Manhattan distance between two points (xi, yi) and (xj, yj) is calculated as |xi - xj| + |yi - yj|.
constraints: At least four distinct integer points lie on the boundary of a square with positive side length.
Choose k points, where 4 <= k <= min(25,len(points)).
Maximize the minimum Manhattan distance between every selected pair.
hints: For candidate distances up to the side length, Manhattan separation of boundary points is equivalent to circular perimeter separation.
Map points clockwise to one coordinate, greedily select the next point at least the candidate gap away, and try every first point.
Reserve a final gap before the perimeter wraps to the start; binary-search the largest feasible gap.
Earliest-next greedy leaves maximum room for remaining selections, and trying every cyclic cut covers every optimal chosen set.
editorial: Earliest-next greedy leaves maximum room for remaining selections, and trying every cyclic cut covers every optimal chosen set.

tests.explanation: Selecting all four corners gives pairwise Manhattan distance at least two.
The best four-point selection has minimum Manhattan distance one.
